type-arguments.comment: Dart's grammar scopes every type name as support.class.dart, so a theme cannot tell CommandHandler apart from the arguments in CommandHandler<A, B>. This injection re-scopes the contents of a type-argument list as support.class.generic.dart so they can be coloured on their own. Handles up to three levels of nesting; the character class rules out comparison expressions.

named-arguments.comment: Dart's grammar gives named arguments (Flutter widget properties like width:, child:) no scope of their own. Tag just the name, never the value. Two forms: the name alone on its line (formatted Flutter), and the name right after ( or , on one line.

property-access.comment: Dart's grammar leaves the segments of a property chain (context.sizing.s80) completely unscoped, so they fall through to the editor foreground. Tag each segment after a dot, but not method calls - those are followed by '(' and the host grammar already scopes them entity.name.function.dart.
